name: Infradex
description: Infradex is an experimental cognitive enhancer that operates on a fundamentally different principle than conventional focus or processing drugs — instead of boosting conscious cognition, it amplifies subconscious parallel processing, allowing the brain's non-conscious problem-solving architecture to work on complex problems while the user performs other tasks or even sleeps. Users report waking with solutions, or suddenly 'knowing' answers to problems they hadn't consciously worked on. Helix positions it as a 'background processing' tool for researchers, strategists, and long-form thinkers.
effects: Insight generation — solutions surface spontaneously during unrelated activity
Enhanced sleep-based memory and problem integration
side_effects: Unsettling sense of thoughts arriving from 'outside' — dissociative ideation
Difficulty trusting consciously derived conclusions (subconscious outputs feel more authoritative)
Vivid, narrative-complex dreams that users struggle to distinguish from memory
Rare: subconscious processing produces intrusive, unwanted problem-solving on traumatic material
Long-term: erosion of conscious deliberative confidence
cultural_context: Infradex is beloved by a certain class of GLMZ intellectual — researchers, architects, long-term strategists, and writers who need insight rather than throughput. It has a cult following in Tier 3 academic circles. The unsettling side effect — the sense of thoughts that feel external — has produced a small but vocal community of Infradex users who have developed quasi-spiritual frameworks around the drug's outputs, treating their subconscious productions as something close to revelation. Helix is watching this community with a mixture of scientific interest and legal concern.
story_hooks: A researcher on extended Infradex use has started producing breakthrough work — but also documenting 'messages' from their subconscious that seem to know things the researcher couldn't possibly know consciously

A character patches Infradex before sleep to subconsciously work a seemingly impossible problem — and wakes knowing the answer, but also knowing something adjacent to it that they were never supposed to figure out

A Helix internal memo leaks suggesting Infradex's subconscious amplification can surface repressed memories — and the company has been quietly tracking which users are producing recall of events Helix would prefer stayed buried
